name: Sign in with Google
plain: One tap sign in with a Google account that is already on the phone.
meaning: Links an app to the person's Google identity (email, name, photo). On Android it reads accounts from the phone through Google Play services without a separate permission.

android.prompt_ui: Bottom sheet listing Google accounts (Credential Manager GetGoogleIdOption)
android.api_surface: androidx.credentials GetGoogleIdOption, Sign in with Google button, AuthorizationClient
android.note: Legacy GoogleSignInClient and One Tap are deprecated in favour of Credential Manager and AuthorizationClient.

ios.prompt_ui: Web auth sheet; system asks to open google.com for sign in
ios.note: Uses a browser flow; no account list from iOS.

limits.headline: Can sign you in with a Google account already on your phone after you tap
limits.user_action: You tap Sign in with Google and choose an account
can: Show the Google accounts on the phone as a picker
Receive your name, email and photo after you pick an account
Create or sign in to an app account without a new password
Ask for more access (such as Drive) with a second approval screen
cannot: List all accounts on your phone without you opening the picker
See your Gmail or Drive files without a separate approval
Show a list of accounts on iPhone; iPhone opens a web sign in instead
limits.differs: Android can show a one tap account picker. iPhone opens a browser sign in and cannot list accounts.

story.what_it_is: One tap signs you into an app with a Google account already on your phone.

marketing.name: Sign in with Google
marketing.pitch: Create an account or sign in with one tap using your Google account instead of a new password.

story.for_you: You see a small sheet at the bottom of the screen with your Google account and a Continue button. One tap and you are in. No new password or email check.
story.for_makers: Makers get fast sign ups and a verified email without building a login system. Google also becomes the middle man that knows which apps you use, and the app can link your account with other apps that use the same login.

use_cases.example: A shopping app lets you join in a tap, so you reach checkout in seconds.
A video or music app uses your Google account so your playlists and history follow you.
A casual game lets you play first, then asks you to sign in with Google to save progress.
A notes or task app creates your account from your Google name and photo.
A delivery app pre fills your email so your first order is faster.
An advertiser links your email from the sign in to the rest of your behavior across the web.

risks: Google sees which apps you use
story.android_note: On Android the account list comes from Google Play services, so no separate permission is needed.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps show a Google web sign in sheet since the phone does not hold Google accounts the same way.

technical_bounds: Needs Play services; not on AOSP only devices

history.change: Credential Manager adds Sign in with Google
Legacy Google Sign-In API deprecated; migration required
